facts: Current local implementation is local-MUSIC-seeded profile residual refinement J(u)=||X-A(u)A(u)^dagger X||_F^2.
Conditional ML/profile-out interpretation requires a declared array manifold and white-noise model; colored noise requires weighting or whitening.
Off-grid and array-error references establish local mismatch and calibration models, but do not validate the exact thesis hardware route.
Calibration-only freeze is supported as a protocol inference; no single cited paper proves the exact 200/200 split.
inferences: Call the method local profile-residual refinement, not a new ML or Bayesian off-grid estimator.

facts: Fully coherent sources make the source covariance rank deficient and can break ordinary covariance-subspace MUSIC/ESPRIT.
Spatial smoothing/FBSS restores usable rank only under ULA/subarray/plane-wave and snapshot assumptions, with aperture loss.
Local SpSF record assumes uncorrelated targets.
Gain/phase/position/mutual-coupling calibration requires an explicit error model and a gauge/reference.
inferences: Direct complex profile fitting, smoothing, and structured covariance are separate routes with separate assumptions.
Noise-free same-range separation cannot be generalized to coherent or mismatched real arrays.
needs_validation: MUSIC versus FBSS versus direct profile residual

facts: Local structural-radar work estimates an LOS-to-structure conversion factor; range-angle vibration work supports angle-gated complex components.
For beta=1/|cos(theta)|, first-order beta sensitivity is approximately beta*tan(theta)*delta_theta away from the cusp.
A phase-reference error contributes approximately lambda*beta*delta_b/(4*pi) under the declared round-trip phase convention.
inferences: Beta is a frozen model parameter for a declared geometry/window, not a universal physical constant.
Angle, reference phase, mounting direction, and mixed-scatterer composition can create multiplicative or additive displacement bias.
needs_validation: angle/beta bias and variance without test-truth tuning

facts: Full GLS uses Sigma including off-diagonal residual correlations; diagonal WLS is a special approximation.
Covariance Intersection gives a conservative route when cross-correlation is unknown.
NIS is an online consistency diagnostic; NEES requires truth and belongs to post-run scoring.
Current P3 innovation correlations are not truth-error covariance and current N_eff is weight diversity only.
inferences: Estimate and freeze Sigma from calibration observables before a full-GLS claim.
CI is a reference for unknown correlation, not evidence of optimal thesis RMSE.
needs_validation: diagonal WLS versus full/block-Sigma GLS versus CI
predeclared NIS interval and empirical coverage

facts: Range-angle component processing can separate same-range targets when finite-aperture/SNR/angle conditions permit.
Coherent sources and cancellation can defeat ordinary covariance peaks or create false peaks.
Local same-range v2 is a bounded synthetic mechanism check, not a universal resolution result.
inferences: split, merge, and abstain must be declared routes tied to identifiability diagnostics.
Unresolved clusters may use an effective beta only when phase stability is demonstrated.
